description: Housing for the busy board PCB v2.0 or v3.0 (v3 factory assembled by JLCPCB; both 222 x 222 mm with the same holes and cut-outs, 247.6 mm square outside) with a clear front: the board is seen through a 3 mm clear polycarbonate plate, cut from a DXF the build exports, held in a black printed frame whose rounded lip covers the plate's cut edge. The plate carries six 24 mm arcade buttons, three panel pots, an EC11-style encoder, three APEM toggles, a slide switch and a small-hole buzzer grille, and has no other openings. A black back tray holds the board on standoffs 15 mm behind the plate and a screwed compartment for the three-cell 14500 LiFePO4 pack, its PCM and the CR-TL24 charger, whose USB-C socket sits recessed in the left wall; a screwed battery door closes it. No fixing or solder joint is reachable from the play side.

hardware.notes: St-John-Software/electronics, hardware/busy-board/ (v2.0) or hardware/busy-board-v3/ (v3.0); dimensions from docs/busy-board/PCB.md and docs/busy-board-v3/PCB.md

Five play buttons and the power button; held by its own panel nut, no push-on cap

hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 482026 (MPN 483363), 24 detents, M7 x 0.5 bushing, 7 mm cut-out (enc_hole_d)
Switch Electronics 486015; 1/4-40 UNS bushing, 6.5 mm cut-out (tgl_hole_d); fixed metal lever, no sealing boot or lever cap
Switch Electronics 490906 (MOQ 10); its tab goes through the plate's tab hole (tgl_lug_r, tgl_lug_d)

hardware.item: On-On slide switch with two screw ears
hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 124002 (MOQ 10); ears 19 mm apart (slide_screw_pitch); actuator part of the switch

hardware.item: CLIFF K15 knob, set-screw fixing, 20 mm
hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 484151 (MPN CL172962); on the pots and the encoder; no push-on knobs

1S3P pack, matched within 50 mV before paralleling; never user-removable

Through the tray floor into the panel posts

printing_notes: Print the frame, tray and door in matte black PETG or ASA, 3 perimeters, without supports: the frame play face down with a brim, the tray floor down, the door outer face down. Frame and tray are 247.6 mm square and need a 250 mm bed (A1). The clear plate is not printed: its STL is for viewing only.

Have the 3 mm clear polycarbonate plate (not acrylic) routed and drilled from https://www.bstjohn.net/3d-models/busy_board_plate.dxf, which the build exports from the OpenSCAD model and draws as seen from the play side. Its only openings are the control, tab, slide-switch and grille holes; keep the protective film on until assembly.
Press the seventeen M3 heat-set inserts before assembly: eight in the frame posts, eight in the tray's PCB posts, one in the door boss.

Assembly order: screw the eight M3 x 15 standoffs through H1-H8 into the tray's PCB posts, which seats the board; fit the buttons, pots, encoder and toggles to the plate with their panel nuts (tabs in their holes), the slide switch with two M2 x 10 screws, 2 mm spacers and nylocs, then the set-screw knobs; drop the plate into the frame's rebate; plug each control lead into the connector beside its cut-out; close up.
The two slide-switch pan-head screws are the one approved play-side fastener besides the control nuts; their nylocs keep them captive. Every other fixing is behind the plate or under the tray.

Tray, by an adult: hot-glue the CR-TL24 into its cradle component side down, sliding it toward the left wall until its USB-C socket passes the pocket's end wall and its charge LEDs sit over the two floor windows. Stick the PCM into its pocket on foam tape. Parallel the three matched cells in their holders, wire them through the PCM to J1 and the charger, and seat the holders in the compartment from the back with the leads through the -X notch.

Close up: frame onto the tray with eight M3 x 10 countersunk screws from the back, which presses the plate onto the standoffs, then the battery door with its M3 x 8. The door needs a screwdriver (adult-only access, cells are never user-removable); J9 is only reachable with the tray off. Charge from the recessed USB-C pocket in the left wall.

The LEDs sit on the board with no spacers, 6.4 mm (v2) / 13.4 mm (v3) behind the clear plate, and no panel diffuses them: re-check their brightness on the bench (BENCH_BRINGUP steps 7.5 and 11.7) before the board goes to the child.

Toggles: the 3 mm plate takes one nut (APEM allows 4 mm with one nut, 2.5 mm with two). Fit each APEM 5636A from behind with the U215 locking ring on its bushing, tab through its plate hole, then the switch's lockwasher and one 8 mm A/F nut on the play face.

VERIFY with the parts in hand: the plate sits flat on the standoffs with no rattle; the control leads reach with the plate held over the board; slide_spacer_h and screw size (M2 assumed: slide_screw_l, slide_head_d, slide_nut_d; the build checks nut and screw clearance); tab holes (pot_lug_a, pot_lug_r, pot_lug_d, tgl_lug_r, tgl_lug_d, enc_lug); the cutting service's minimum hole (1.5 mm assumed) and that it accepts 64-sided polylines instead of CIRCLEs.

VERIFY against the delivered parts and adjust: arcade button depth, nut and switch reach (button_depth, button_nut_d, button_switch_reach); the toggle face and depth (tgl_face_d, tgl_depth); and the pot and encoder depths (pot_depth, enc_depth).

VERIFY the pack side too: cell holder size (batt_l, batt_w, batt_h); PCM size (pcm_l, pcm_w); the CR-TL24 outline, seat height and LED positions (chg_l, chg_w, chg_seat, chg_led) and its USB-C plug overmould (usb_pocket_d); and the JST-XH lead room (raising pcb_to_panel needs longer standoffs: standoff_l).

wall, corner_r, edge_r, inner_d, insert_hole_d and lip_clear are shared by the frame and the tray, panel_t by the frame and the plate, and floor_t, batt_l, batt_w, door_t and door_clear by the tray and the door: set them identically on every part that exposes them.
